subject: MAP sync: unit-econ checks, eval plan, and proposed close timeline for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Sasha Cohen <sasha.cohen@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — unit econ details and traffic profile

Hi Rachel / team,

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalizing our mutual action plan (MAP) and need a focused review on unit economics assumptions so procurement and finance can sign off. Key ask: can Redwood validate the tokens-per-call and batching/caching assumptions in the attached simulation file and confirm what acceptance gates you'd expect for the MAP?

Quick context:
- Product: customer support triage + answer synthesis (mix of short prompts + long context retrieval)
- Peak concurrent users (internal estimate): 180 requests/sec for the primary region; average 75 rps across the day
- Typical average prompt size (incl. system + history): ~420 tokens; average completion 220 tokens
- SLA target: P95 latency <= 450ms for streaming responses

Attached: token-econ-sim.csv (sample traffic buckets) and a draft MAP doc (aurelia_map_draft_v1.docx).

Questions we need answered for our MAP signoff:
1) Tokens/$ projection at our traffic profile assuming Redwood hosted and a dedicated cache warmup
2) Expected effect of prefix caching for 25% of requests (reduction in generated tokens)
3) Guidance on batching window to preserve P95 latency while maximizing tokens per GPU-dollar
4) Recommended eval plan (sim timeline + acceptance criteria) to include in the MAP

Can we get a short readout by EOD Tuesday (PST)? Procurement is pushing for the MAP to include explicit unit-econ gates.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-minute call if helpful.

— Sasha
Sasha Cohen
Head of Platform Integrations, Aurelia Health
[sender phone redacted]

[Attachment: aurelia_map_draft_v1.docx (DOCX, 78KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Cohen <sasha.cohen@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit econ details and traffic profile

Thanks Sasha — got the files and the high-level profile. Quick confirmation below and a proposed next step plan.

Short answers up front:
- We can validate the tokens/$ assumption and produce a 7-day sim using your CSV buckets plus a small set of traffic perturbations.
- Prefix caching for ~25% of requests typically reduces generated tokens by ~15-30% depending on prompt variability; we'll model conservatively at 18% in the MAP.
- Batching: to keep P95 latency <= 450ms in hosted mode we recommend a 5–8ms batching window with a dynamic batch-size cap (depends on model choice) — we'll include exact numbers in the sim.

What we'll deliver by Tue EOD (our time):
- A short unit-econ memo with tokens-per-dollar for 3 model/quantization profiles (base, q4x, int8-like), using your traffic CSV as baseline.
- A clear set of acceptance gates for the MAP: throughput (sustained RPS), P95 latency, and cost per 1M requests delta vs baseline (>10% improvement target to accept MAP).
- An eval plan: smoke sim (3 days), full sim (7 days), and a short live pilot (48–72 hours) with monitoring dashboards.

Clarifying questions (please reply inline if possible):
1) When you say 25% prefix caching, is that mostly identical system prompts (same template) or variable user history?
2) Do you expect long-context retrieval to be fetched pre-request (so included in the request token count) or as an enrichment step on our side?
3) Procurement target for cost: do you have a target tokens/$ (or $/1M requests) threshold we should treat as the MAP budget gate?

Proposed next steps after our memo: 30-minute MAP alignment call where we walk the sim outputs and lock dates for the smoke sim + pilot. I'm free Tue 3–4pm PST or Wed 10–11am PST.

Cheers,

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0143

[Attachment: Redwood_token-econ-playbook.pdf (stub: generated reference, 12KB)]

From: Danielle Park <dpark@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Cohen <sasha.cohen@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit econ details and traffic profile

Thanks Rachel — answers below.

Inline to your questions:
> 1) When you say 25% prefix caching, is that mostly identical system prompts (same template) or variable user history?
Mostly identical system prompts + FAQ-style scaffolding. About half of that 25% are identical system prompts; the rest are repeated user queries (same phrasing) where cache hits are realistic.

> 2) Do you expect long-context retrieval to be fetched pre-request (so included in the request token count) or as an enrichment step on our side?
We plan to do retrieval on our side and include the retrieved context in the request payload (so yes, count those tokens). Retrieval size varies (avg 1,100 tokens when included).

> 3) Procurement target for cost: do you have a target tokens/$ (or $/1M requests) threshold we should treat as the MAP budget gate?
Procurement is looking for a baseline comparable to our existing vendor: they want <= $X per 1M output tokens (we'll keep that internal for now); for the MAP they will accept up to a 12% delta above that if the latency/RTO targets are met.

Additional notes:
- Peak concurrency may spike to 260 rps for brief bursts during ETL syncs; our traffic CSV includes sample bursts but we flagged them as 2% of total traffic.
- Procurement would like the eval plan to include a simple cost-reconciliation step: expected spend vs actual spend during pilot compared over 72 hours.

We can join the call Tue 3:30pm PST — Sasha, can you confirm?

— Danielle
Danielle Park
Sr. Product Ops, Aurelia Health

[Attachment: sample_traffic_buckets_v2.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Cohen <sasha.cohen@aureliahealth.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit econ details and traffic profile

Thanks — this is helpful. Below is a concise MAP excerpt we propose to include in the doc and the owners/dates. I'll upload an updated MAP with these gates.

Proposed MAP excerpt (for insertion into aurelia_map_draft_v1.docx):
- Objective: Validate Redwood-hosted inference at Aurelia traffic profile with unit-econ gates for procurement signoff.
- Acceptance gates (all must pass for final MAP approval):
  * Sustained throughput: >= 70 rps sustained for 24 hours in the pilot region (allowing for 2% 10-min burst to 260 rps)
  * Latency: P95 <= 450ms for streaming responses during pilot windows
  * Cost gate: Measured cost per 1M output tokens <= (procurement baseline + 12%)
  * Cache effectiveness: Measured reduction in generated tokens for cached class >= 15%

Milestones & owners (proposed):
- Tue 2027-05-11: Redwood memo + tokens/$ sims delivered (owner: Rachel) — DONE
- Wed 2027-05-12: MAP draft updated with gates + timelines (owner: Aurelia)
- Fri 2027-05-14 – Mon 2027-05-17: Smoke sim (3 days) and initial readout (owner: Redwood ops: Marcus)
- Tue 2027-05-18 – Thu 2027-05-20: Full 7-day sim (owner: Redwood ops: Marcus)
- Fri 2027-05-21 – Sun 2027-05-23: Live pilot (72 hours) and cost reconciliation (owner: Aurelia ops)
- Mon 2027-05-24: MAP decision meeting (final accept/adjust)

Open items we will include in the updated MAP doc:
- Exact batching window numbers per model (we'll send per-model sims by Wed morning)
- Baseline tokens/$ tables for three quant profiles and recommended production profile for cost/latency tradeoff
- Acceptance dashboard links (we'll share a live dashboard during pilot)
- DocuSign link for a pilot SOW draft — Danielle, can you share the procurement contact or a PO template we should attach?

If that timeline looks good I'll push the updated MAP to your Drive and add the acceptance dashboards. Short call Tue 3:30pm PST works — I'll send a calendar invite shortly.

-r

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
